Now let me read the part index to narrow candidates.

Leaf candidates: Bacterial_Canker, Bacterial_Speck, Cucumber_Mosaic, Early_Blight, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Phytophthora_Blight, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

Top candidates based on the grayish-brown velvety necrosis: **Gray_Mold**, **Late_Blight**, **Leaf_Mold**, **Phytophthora_Blight**. Viewing one reference from each.
This Late Blight reference is very similar to the test image - large brown necrotic area with green portions remaining, on a gray surface. Let me check the other candidates.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Gray Mold** reference: Shows tan/brown necrotic patches but lacks the grayish-brown velvety sporulation mass visible on the test image
- **Late Blight** (CDDM_498): Very strong match - same gray background surface, large irregular brown necrotic area covering majority of leaf with green portions remaining, papery/dry texture, nearly identical visual presentation to the test image
- **Leaf Mold**: Discrete pale yellow spots pattern - does not match at all
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Shows water-soaked, collapsed brownish area but with a more saturated/wet appearance, less papery

The test image most closely matches **Late_Blight**: large irregular brown necrotic lesion covering most of the leaf surface, remaining green areas, papery dry texture, laid flat on a gray surface - exactly matching the CDDM_498 reference.
